_comment: Assembly order of the BENCH pod (water only, never on a person) as data, derived from mechanical/ASSEMBLY.md (B-sections) and docs/build-guide/03..09. Read by check_assembly.py. Body names are the SolidCraft body names of out/bench/<size>.sc (bodies that do not exist in a CAD revision are skipped; CAD bodies not mentioned here are reported). 'path' = list of straight segments IN ASSEMBLY ORDER, ending at the CAD position: the part starts at (CAD position - sum(dir*dist)) and moves along dir. 'parts' entries '@ctx' = everything assembled so far in sub-assembly context ctx. 'engages' = pairs that are INTENDED to touch/overlap: kind press (tolerated inside 'zone' mm of the CAD position), snap / stretch (elastic, tolerated everywhere, deflection measured), flexible (the part is a flexible cable: threading needed, reported as a note). All directions are world axes: X = pod length (+X = dock mouth), Y = width, Z = up.

driver._comment: owner's spec: tip D1.5 / D2.0, shaft D3, handle D12 beyond 15 mm. tip_len = length of the narrow tip section (assumption: 2.0 mm; the checker also reports the minimum tip length that would clear).

tweezers._comment: approach cone behind the part; the tweezers may come in tilted up to max_tilt_deg from the axis opposite the insertion direction (any azimuth); OK if one approach has a free cone of the given half angle

M1.2._comment: head_h = counterbore depth (params screws.head_depth 0.5): worst case head flush with the counterbore floor + 0.5

steps.title: Rear seal ring A stretched over the core into the rear groove
Front seal ring B stretched over the core into the front groove
Printed nose disc glued on the plunger front face
M1.6 nut dropped into the carriage hex pocket
Steel tongue shim glued into the carriage pocket
Thrust sleeve into gear B (carriage side)
Plunger (core + rings + nose) pushed into the reservoir from the open dry end
End cap spigot pressed into the reservoir port
Fill septum plug pressed into the cap side bore
Duckbill valve dropped into the open cap slot and pressed into its pocket
Valve plug pressed into the slot (flush with the cap top)
Dry bush pressed into the dry-end bearing bore
Far bush pressed into the wet-end bearing bore
Reservoir sub-assembly (reservoir, plunger, cap, septum, valve) lowered into the shell
Carriage sub-assembly lowered onto the rail, then slid -Y so the shim enters the plunger socket
Gear B + sleeve lowered into the gear plane
Leadscrew inserted from the dock end through far bush, nut, sleeve, dry bush
Motor (gearbox, shaft, boss, terminal block, pins) laid into the three cradles
Gear A slid onto the motor D-shaft from the dry end
Thrust collar slid on the rod end
Spindle magnet glued on the rod end face
Needle + hub pressed into the cap guard tube from the dock mouth
Pod sensor board lowered onto posts and locating pins
FFC cable pushed into the ZIF connector (flip lock) from the +X side
Gasket laid on the bottom tongue
Lid lowered straight down (FFC cable through its slot)
Dock insert slid into the dock window from the +X mouth until the detents click
Dock magnet d2x1 glued into the rear lug pocket of the dummy head
Dock: dummy head pushed into the pod mouth, snap arms spread and latch behind the dome

proposals.title: Re-ordering inside the current CAD: gear A on the shaft before the motor is lowered (meshing from above), dock insert before the board, gasket before the FFC cable

new_steps.title: Motor with gear A already pressed on the shaft, lowered into the cradles and meshed with gear B

fix_hints.M4: Verified by two extra sweeps: lowered straight down the carriage itself is free, but the shim (z 3.5..4.9, y 17.5..21.5) hits the reservoir wall above the arm slot (the slot is a closed window z 3.4..5.0, wall above it up to z 7.5) and the plunger top; sliding the carriage in from +Y is impossible because the cradle/lane wall at y 24.9..26.9 (z <= 2.12) leaves no room. No order fixes this. Make the arm slot open to the top (slot cut from the reservoir top face down to z 3.4; the CNC drawing is frozen, so decide before ordering), or glue the shim into the plunger socket and give the carriage a top-open pocket, or move to the push-rod concept of docs/REVIEW-2026-11-19.md (no carriage, no shim).
fix_hints.M5: Gear B with its sleeve (tail x 1.95..2.6) cannot be lowered: the dry bearing block (x up to 2.55, top z 6.38) covers the sleeve tail; sliding the sleeve in afterwards is impossible (carriage bore d1.9 < sleeve OD 2.0, and only 0.5 mm between gear B and the carriage). Use open-top (U) bearing cradles or end the sleeve tail at x >= 2.6, with the thrust shoulder moved to a ring on the rod.
fix_hints.M6: The 25 mm rod cannot be inserted from the dock end. Rays along the rod axis (y 22.5, z 4.2) hit solid at x 0..0.9 (dry-end wall: no entry from outside), x 32.0..33.6 (board support post POST1, centre 32.8/22.4), x 42.4..43.6 (board pin / post) and the end wall x 46.1..47.0; the free cavity from the far bush (x 25.6) to the end wall (x 46.1) is 20.5 mm, shorter than the rod (25 mm), so the rod would have to pass through the end wall as well. Options: (a) through-bore in the dry-end wall: rod from outside, bush pressed in from outside afterwards, closing plug; (b) open-top (U) bearing cradles so rod + carriage + gear B + sleeve + bushes go in as one module from above (the lid pads hold it down); (c) in any case move the board posts/pins off the rod axis (y 22.5). For OP-70 (rod 21 mm) the same walls apply.
fix_hints.M8: Sliding gear A onto the shaft needs x 1.0..2.4 free next to the dry-end wall; the wall region x 0.6..2.0 overlaps (7.1 mm3). Tested alternative X1 (section 2a): fit gear A on the shaft first and lower motor + gear A together, meshing with gear B.
fix_hints.M16: Two separate collisions. (1) After the board is fitted the front block of the dock insert (z up to 5.2) hits the dock-hall chip on the board (hall_dock, z 4.9..5.3, x 43.25..44.35, 0.3 mm deep): fit the insert before the board (tested, X1), or keep the insert top <= 4.8 mm, or move the chip. (2) Even before the board (X1) a 0.25 mm collision remains: the insert's flange band at z 0.5..0.75 (y 3.7..18.7) meets a floor rib of the bottom at x 32.95..33.45 while it slides in: add a lead-in/lower the rib by 0.3 mm. Also the dock mouth has 0.05 mm skins (x 46.95..47.0, bottom z 4.95..5.0 and lid z 5.01..5.2, reported as grazing): open the mouth cleanly.
fix_hints.A1: The dock-magnet pocket (d2.1 at x 43.8) overlaps the dome rim: the dome edge at x 43.2 leaves a 0.4 mm lip above z 4.4 over the pocket's -X side, so the magnet cannot be dropped in vertically. Move the pocket +0.5 mm in X (or lower the dome rim there) and re-check hall alignment.
fix_hints.D1: Grazing only (0.1 mm): the dome top (z 5.0) touches the dock-hall chip underside (z 4.9). Raise the board/chip or lower the dome by 0.2 mm.
fix_hints.M14: The FFC cable (already connected) lies across the gasket ring: lift the cable or fit the gasket before the cable (tested in X1); the closed 8.0 x 1.1 mm lid window needs the cable end threaded through before the lid goes down: document this in 08.3 or open the window at the bottom (notch from the lid rim).

fix_general: **Tolerance reality check (all printed fits).** JLC3DP quotes SLA +-0.2 mm (holes +-0.3 mm) and MJF +-0.3 mm (holes +-0.3 mm) and says holes shrink; the CAD/sim assume SLA +-0.05 and MJF +-0.10, the fab README orders +-0.1 / +-0.2. With the vendor numbers most 0.02..0.1 mm press/slip fits in section 5 are a lottery as printed. Either design to the vendor clearances (SLA 0.2 assembled / 0.5 moving, MJF 0.2-0.4 / 0.6) or make the finishing step (ream, drill, sand, brass part) an explicit build-guide step per pair, and order a bore/pin calibration coupon first to measure the real `hole_bias`.

**End cap (SLA).** The d4.2 septum bore sits in a block of only 4.4 x 4.3 mm (x 25.8..30.2, z 0.9..5.2), i.e. 0.1 mm walls, and the bore is tangent to the cap's bottom face (bore axis z 3.0, radius 2.1, face z 0.9): zero-thickness skins over about 1300 samples, i.e. a probable hole through the cap floor. Make the block >= 5.4 mm wide and move the bore axis up >= 0.5 mm, or use a smaller plug. The d0.7 channels (up to 17 mm long, three jogs) are beyond the vendor hole table (d1.0 only to 3 mm deep): they cannot be printed or flushed; use straight drilled channels or inserted tubing.

**Carriage / plunger core (SLA).** Sub-0.1 mm knife edges at the end of the shim pocket (carriage y 21.6) and at the plunger socket edge (z 4.85..5.05, y 18.85): remove the tiny steps; the 0.55 mm shim pocket (vendor minimum 1.0 mm) and the 0.24 mm walls beside it are below the SLA hard floor 0.4 mm: widen the carriage near the pocket or make the shim pocket a cut-out through a thicker boss.

**MJF housings (bottom, top, dock fixture).** 0.05 mm membranes at the dock mouth (x 46.95..47.0) and at the motor floor relief (z 0.35, x 18..24, y 25..28), slots of 0.2-0.6 mm (dry-end wall at x 1.0..2.4) and 0.4-0.5 mm shell walls are below the MJF hard floor 0.5 mm; 95 % of the wall area is thinner than JLC3DP's recommended 1.4-1.5 mm. Expect the vendor DFM review to reject or thicken them: raise walls to >= 0.8 mm where space allows, delete the membranes, and keep M1.2 pilots/clearance holes (d1.0 / d1.4 < vendor minimum 1.5 mm) as drilled features (already in the build guide).

**Thrust sleeve and collar (SLA).** Wall 0.2 mm (sleeve) and 0.4 mm (collar) are below the SLA hard floor: use the brass tube versions (the fab README already prefers them) and drop the printed files from the order.

**CNC reservoir (PP).** Wall 0.8 mm is below the JLCCNC absolute minimum for plastics (1.0 mm; 1.5 mm recommended) on all three sizes; PCBWay's own limit was not found, ask them before the order. The arm slot (1.6 mm) needs a small end mill, the D5 tool only makes the R2.5 bore ends; OP-200's bore depth/D is 6.5 (special long-reach tool, see the CNC README).
